business_problem: DXC's security operations center was facing rapidly growing cyber complexity, including zero-day vulnerabilities, identity-based attacks, supply chain breaches, and AI-enabled adversary tactics, while analyst shortages and repetitive triage work were straining teams and slowing response.
solution_summary: DXC describes an internally built AI-driven transformation of its security operations center in which AI agents were developed and deployed across the SOC to automate repetitive front-line security work. The implementation focused on ticket triage, investigation support, and broader agentic protection workflows rather than a broad platform replacement. DXC says it introduced the agents through a controlled MVP approach, validating the model on smaller deployments, gathering feedback, then scaling across operations. In practice, the agents handle tedious triage work continuously, while human analysts provide judgment, oversight, and guardrail management for agent actions. The operating model integrates AI into existing SOC processes and talent workflows so analysts can move from Tier 1 repetitive work toward threat intelligence and threat hunting. The source does not name specific storage, model, or cloud components, so the described architecture is best understood as an in-house AI agent layer embedded into DXC's SOC workflow and analyst operating processes.

solution_components.name: AI agents
solution_components.role: They automate repetitive SOC work such as ticket triage and support investigation workflows so analysts can focus on higher-value security tasks.

business_outcome: DXC reports materially faster SOC response and investigation workflows, full elimination of reliance on Tier 1 analysts for repetitive triage tasks, and the ability to redeploy staff into higher-value work such as threat intelligence analysis and threat hunting.
